subject: Gradual deprecation — communication gates, SLA for exceptions, and customer pacing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc:  
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Gradual deprecation — communication gates, SLA for exceptions, and customer pacing

Team —

Following product leadership’s decision to consolidate the model family for the v1 text endpoints, I want us to align on a deprecation cadence that protects high-risk customers and gives Sales/CS and Infra clear gates for exceptions. This thread is to capture the operational model, proposed timeline, and who owns the customer-facing comms. I attached a first-pass runbook (deprecation_runbook_v1.pdf).

High-level proposal (draft):
- Phase 1 (60 days notice): public blog + docs note; opt-in compatibility shim for 30 days.
- Phase 2 (30 days after Phase 1): disable legacy endpoint for new traffic; grandfathered customers remain on a flagged path.
- Phase 3 (final 30 days): full cutover for all non-exempt accounts.

Exception gating:
- Sales can request an exception with a mutual action plan (MAP) and committed dates.
- Exceptions carry an SLA: enable for up to 90 days with a single 30-day grace extension (requires POD lead signoff).

Asks by role:
- Ben (Sales): confirm acceptable exception SLA and a short template for MAPs; we need an escalation ladder for large deals (>$250k ARR).
- Monica (CS): finalize customer notice wording and the early technical checklist (logs, SDK notes).
- Rishi (Infra): confirm the operational cost of running the compatibility shim and what load we can sustain concurrently with normal traffic.
- Priyom (Ops): define the rollout automation hooks and reporting we’ll need in Console to show exempted customers.

Key constraints: we must avoid rolling back customer traffic that depends on old tokenization or embed shape changes — those need longer transition windows.

Please reply with your redlines and commitments by EOD Monday so I can lock timelines for comms.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, API Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gradual deprecation — communication gates, SLA for exceptions

Marissa — thanks for the clear framing. A few constraints from Sales and field:

1) SLA for exceptions: the proposed 90-day window + one 30-day extension is reasonable for mid-market accounts, but for Strategic deals (Quantico Labs, EdgeCloud) we need a path for a 6-month engineered migration tied to a MAP. Can we make the "SLA" tiered: standard (90+30) vs strategic (case-by-case with exec sponsor)?

2) MAP template: I attached a skeleton MAP in the XLSX for Quantico (quantico_map_mutual_action_plan.xlsx). For large deals we need an explicit billing hold and a weekly ops sync cadence itemized in the MAP.

3) Comms cadence: Sales requests a private early-warning email 45 days before Phase 1 announcement for accounts we flagged as at-risk (we already have a list in HubSpot: HS-927421). Public blog timing should follow that private notice by 10 days to avoid churn.

4) Escalation ladder: for >$250k ARR we want a direct channel to go to Partnerships + Product + Legal; add "Head of Sales" as a contact in the MAP.

I can get partner exec buy-in for Quantico if the MAP and timeline are acceptable. If not, we push for a longer runway.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Short technical constraints from Infra:

- Compatibility shim cost: running the shim for ~200 flagged accounts concurrently will add roughly 10-12% additional GPU load at peak for the first 30 days; after that the incremental cost drops as prefixes expire. We can absorb this in Hosted for Q3 but not sustained beyond 90 days without either dedicated pool assignment or cost-pass to the customer.

- Operational hooks: we need a Console flag to mark exempted customers and an automated metric that reports prefix-hit rates by customer. Priyom + I can ship a minimal flag + metric in 3 sprints (6 weeks) if we deprioritize a few other infra items.

- Risk: tokenization/shape changes are high-risk. If Quantico requires legacy tokenization for longer than 90 days, we need a migration engineer embedded on their MAP (Ben, you mentioned that).

I'll add a short appendix with load estimates to the drive link today.

Rishi
